A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDO research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDO evaluations on DXY, GMD, and CMD, including component ablations, confidence-estimation comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports macro-F1/micro-F1 results, confidence intervals, and paired significance tests.

M1.justification: The four-agent architecture, objectives, and consultation procedure remain unchanged. However, Appendix A.2 revises the stated training workflow: v1 selects the best diagnostic adapter before policy training, whereas v2 trains policies using several retained Qwen2.5-7B adapter checkpoints and selects the final policy afterward. Joint optimization remains a future proposal.

E1.justification: Both versions use DXY, GMD, and CMD for the same simulated medical-consultation task. The reported splits and augmented calibration-set sizes are unchanged; v2's additional original sample counts do not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains EBAD, MTDiag, HAIformer, DP, UoT, and CoD, and Table 4 retains the same confidence-estimation comparators. The new F1 and significance comparisons reuse HAIformer. Diaformer is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds macro-F1 and micro-F1 evaluation in Section 5.9. The reported GMD RL-policy window changes from 4 in v1 Table 6 to 5 in v2 Table 7, while the collaborative-inquiry window remains 4 in v2 Table 8. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.9 adds a macro-F1/micro-F1 comparison with HAIformer to examine diagnostic balance across disease classes. The existing component ablations, maximum-turn sensitivity analysis, disease-level plot, and appendix consultation case are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B expands from means and standard errors to include 95% confidence intervals and paired t-tests against HAIformer across all three datasets. It also removes the initial-accuracy uncertainty row and replaces the explicit three-seed statement with an unspecified number of different seeds. The expanded statistical reporting does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Most existing results remain unchanged. Table 2 revises HAIformer's DXY/GMD/CMD average turns from 1.7/2.0/3.4 to 1.8/1.9/3.6 and CMD accuracy from 70.9 to 71.1. Appendix B replaces the DXY summary of 85.3 ± 1.1 with mean 84.4 and standard error 0.8. v2 additionally reports F1 scores, confidence intervals, and p-values; these do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, state/action definitions, confidence calculation, calibration loss, reward expression, and sampling equations remain unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical proofs, and v2 introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace independent optimization with the narrower formulation of optimization using distinct objectives, consistent with the discussion of cascaded training. The central four-agent contribution and claims of outperforming LLM baselines while remaining competitive with generation-based methods are retained.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands discussion of action-space difficulty, remedies for poorly ranked diseases, cascaded-training instability, potential joint optimization, and inference overhead with trajectory reuse. Section 5.9 and Appendix B add interpretations about class balance, repeatability, and scaling to more disease categories. The earlier deployment, label-granularity, and latency limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a DDO code-access statement, UoT and CoD parameter values, original calibration sample counts, floor-turn and retry settings, and a typical consultation time of 3–5 minutes. It removes the explicit incomplete-case filtering description and do_sample=False disclosure. Hardware and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Diaformer to the generative-method discussion and bibliography. It also connects the proposed trajectory-memory remedy to the already cited Chopra and Shah work. The broader positioning against prior medical-consultation approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and selected passages, adds Discussion and Acknowledgments sections, expands Appendix A.2, and subdivides Appendix B. These are localized structural and explanatory additions; most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds F1 and significance-test tables, restructures the uncertainty table, and separates RL-policy settings from collaborative-inquiry settings. Figure 4 moves to the right column, while the existing figures retain their content. The overall two-column design and appendix case/prompt layouts remain.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical transparency through additional settings, a code-access statement, and specific discussion of training instability and inference cost. However, the new statistical evidence omits the seed count and leaves the F1 backbone/run setting and corresponding paired HAIformer results insufficiently specified. Consequently, the paired-test claim of a DXY advantage cannot be reliably checked against matching summaries. These benefits and reporting gaps prevent a confident net quality judgment.
